chapter.title: Food Industry Residues and Prepared Animal Feed

page.h1: HTS Chapter 23: Food Industry Residues and Prepared Animal Feed — Export Markets & Foreign Tariffs on U.S. Goods

seo.title: Chapter 23 Export Markets: Tariffs on U.S. Soybean Meal, DDGS & Pet Food by Country
seo.shortDescription: What Canada, Mexico, Colombia, Viet Nam, China, the EU and other buyers charge on U.S. soybean meal, DDGS, pet food and animal feed, and whose approval is needed to sell there.

intro: For most of this chapter the tariff is not what decides a sale. The two biggest buyers, Canada and Mexico, take U.S. pet food, soybean meal and DDGS duty-free under USMCA; Colombia and Korea do the same under their U.S. agreements; and Viet Nam, the Philippines and Japan charge little or nothing even at MFN rates. China is the exception: its 10% extra tariff applies on top of every line, and anti-dumping and countervailing duties keep U.S. DDGS out almost entirely. Pet food is the product group that pays the most where there is no agreement (15% in China, 9.6% or a per-tonne duty in the EU outside its new U.S. quota). Everywhere, access for pet food and animal-origin feed depends on the buyer’s veterinary approval, named on each card.
valueBasis: FOB value of U.S. exports, as reported by the United States to UN Comtrade.

profile.headline: Canada is the largest buyer, mostly of U.S. pet food and prepared feed, and it pays no duty on qualifying goods under CUSMA. Its March 2025 counter-tariff list caught only one niche line, dairy-based feed above Canada’s access quota, and that was removed on September 1, 2025.

assumptions: Rates are what U.S.-origin goods pay in 2026. For the EU they come from the 2026 Combined Nomenclature (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1926); for the other markets, from the MFN applied rates each country reported to the WTO/World Bank WITS (TRAINS) database for 2023, its latest reported year, with any 2025–2026 change on U.S. goods added from the official text.

Each cell covers a whole four-digit heading, so it shows the range across its six-digit lines and names the main line where they differ (soybean meal 2304.00, DDGS 2303.30, dog and cat food 2309.10, other prepared feed 2309.90).

Trade-agreement rates (USMCA/CUSMA, the Colombia TPA, KORUS) apply only to goods that meet the agreement’s rules of origin; the normal (MFN) rate is shown beside them. For Colombia and Korea, the phase-out status of individual feed lines was taken from the agreements’ summaries; check the trade.gov FTA Tariff Tool for the exact line.

China’s 10% extra tariff on U.S. goods, its anti-dumping and countervailing duties on DDGS and its 2018–19 counter-tariffs are added on top of the MFN rate; their history and dates are on Tariff updates.
National 8–10-digit lines, specific (per-tonne) duties and quota rates can differ from the ranges shown; check the market’s own schedule before relying on this page for a transaction.
